input: Shred five years of old financial documents at home

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Financial documents vary widely — knowing which types are included (tax returns, bank statements, medical bills, receipts, pay stubs, etc.) determines the volume and whether any should be kept rather than shredded.
The volume of documents dictates whether a home shredder is practical or whether a professional shredding service would be faster and more cost-effective.
Whether the user owns a shredder, and its capacity (strip-cut vs. cross-cut, sheet capacity), directly determines the immediate next action and how long the job will take.
Knowing where the documents are stored (filing cabinet, boxes, loose piles) affects how much pre-sorting and organisation is needed before shredding can begin.
If a partner, spouse, or family member co-owns the finances, they may need to be involved in decisions about what to keep vs. destroy.
The user may want a fully paperless result (scanning before shredding), or simply to reduce clutter — this changes the workflow significantly.
Some users want to do this in one focused session; others prefer to spread it across several sessions — this shapes how the task should be broken into steps.

gold.taskTitle: Shred five years of home financial documents
gold.taskDescription: Sort through and securely destroy five years' worth of personal financial documents stored at home.

questions.title: Which document types are you shredding — all or specific categories?
questions.description: Identify whether the scope covers everything (bank statements, tax returns, pay stubs, receipts, medical bills) or only certain document types, since some records should legally be kept longer.

questions.title: Roughly how many boxes or folders of documents are there?
questions.description: Estimate the total volume so we can determine whether a home shredder session is realistic or a drop-off / pick-up shredding service makes more sense.

questions.title: Do you already own a shredder, and if so what type?
questions.description: Knowing whether a shredder is available (and whether it is strip-cut, cross-cut, or micro-cut) determines the immediate first step and sets realistic expectations for speed.

questions.title: Where are the documents stored — filed, boxed, or scattered?
questions.description: Understanding the current storage state reveals how much gathering and pre-sorting is needed before any shredding can begin.

questions.title: Does anyone else need to sign off on what gets destroyed?
questions.description: Determine whether a partner, spouse, or co-filer needs to be consulted before documents are permanently destroyed.

questions.title: Do you want to scan and save digital copies before shredding?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is purely to destroy paper or to go paperless by digitising records first, since this adds a significant step to the workflow.

questions.title: Do you want to finish this in one session or spread it out?
questions.description: Understand the user's preferred pace so the plan can be structured as a single focused block of time or a series of shorter, manageable sessions.
